summary: Carry the two .xlsx parser fixtures as base64 text sidecars and decode them in a readFixture test helper, instead of committing the raw ZIP-container spreadsheets.
reason: The public printing-press-library CI job 'Block committed MCPB/native binary payloads' (.github/scripts/verify-binary-payload/verify_binary_payload.py) rejects any newly added file under library/ whose first bytes are the ZIP magic PK\x03\x04, and it has no exemption for testdata. .xlsx is a ZIP container, so both fixtures failed the Verify check. The guard's stated rationale is that MCPB and native release binaries must be built from source in Actions rather than committed; these files are neither, they are upstream source spreadsheets used as parser fixtures. Dropping them instead would have deleted the PDF-vs-XLSX cross-encoding assertion, which is the CLI's only measurement of extraction quality taken from outside the extractor, so they are base64-encoded rather than removed. readFixture still prefers a raw fixture when one is present, so a local tree holding the original binaries behaves identically.
validated_outcome: base64 round-trip verified byte-identical against the raw .xlsx before the raw files were deleted. go test -race ./... passes with zero failures, and TestPDFAgreesWithXLSX still runs (not skipped) and reproduces the pre-change numbers exactly: compared=2601 value-agree=2580 value-disagree=0 flagged-overflow-loss=21 missing=0 coverage=100.00%, description fidelity exact=2142 flagged-suspect=459 silent-bad=0 (82.4%). gofmt clean, go vet exit 0.
